Prevention: Bacterial blight of coffee (BBC) can be a serious problem at high altitudes where heavy winds injure plants; plant shade trees and wind breaks on exposed sides of
BBC areas to avoid the spreading of the disease
Use clean disease-free planting material, avoid planting material from known
Monitoring: Carefully monitor symptoms, particularly during cool wet weather which favours the bacterium:
Initial symptoms: necrosis of nodes, internodes and shoot tips, often accompanied by necrosis of the petiole and basal part of the leaf, spreading rapidly on primary branches
Leaves dry up and roll inwards turning brown, but remain attached
Affected plantations have a fire-scorched appearance
BBC differ from symptoms of typical halo blight of coffee which are more restricted to the leaves
Direct Control: Cut off infected twigs, at least 5 cm from the point of infection, and collect them in buckets.
Destroy by burning or burying away from the field
Disinfect tools and implements with 70% alcohol after pruning infected trees or cutting twigs
After heavy outbreaks, destroy infected trees
